content.comment_body: Hello, I'm interested to know if anyone has managed to upload multiple [product_name] devices from different remote locations into a single AWS cloud account (as device 1, device 2, and so on)? My current project involves up to 20 remotely located [product_name] units and I want to confirm whether it’s feasible to centralize each web server within a single AWS account. Thanks in advance.

I haven't used the AWS function myself, but my understanding is that the web browser interface shifts to the cloud with some modifications. As a result, it's not possible to merge individual [product_name] web servers with different addresses into one AWS account.
Thanks for your reply. That's what I suspected—I just wanted to verify my understanding.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are interested in centralizing remote access to several [product_name] web servers from different sites using a single AWS cloud account. The main issue discussed is that separate web servers, each with a distinct address, cannot be merged under one AWS cloud account using the current cloud solution, which poses challenges for scalability and unified management of distributed installations.
analysis.user_expectations: Forum users are looking for an easy way to aggregate and manage multiple [product_name] devices' web servers from various locations in one centralized AWS account, aiming for streamlined administration and access.
